target.title: fix(agents): preserve runtime tool inheritance tokens for spawned subagents (#85030)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #85030: MCP/LSP/plugin tools not injected into subagent (sessions_spawn) sessions.

Deferred runtime selectors (`bundle-mcp`, `server__tool`, `lsp_*`, `group:plugins`) materialize into concrete tools only at runtime (MCP servers connect async, LSP/plugin tools build lazily). When a spawned subagent inherits the parent's effective tool surface via `replaceWithEffectiveToolAllowlist`, these selectors were absent from the synchronous concrete parent tool array and were silently dropped. The child then received only built-in tools, breaking multi-agent orchestration where worker agents need MCP/LSP/plugin tools.

### Root Cause

In all three spawn paths (`createOpenClawCodingTools`, `resolveGatewayScopedTools`, `resolveSkillDispatchTools`), the inherited allowlist was populated exclusively from concrete parent tools. Deferred selectors like `bundle-mcp` or `probe__search` have no concrete tool counterpart in the synchronous tool array, so they were dropped — even though the parent's policy explicitly authorized them.

### Fix

1. **Identify** deferred selectors with `isRuntimeMaterializationAllowlistEntry`
2. **Expand** each selector to its umbrella policy names (e.g. `probe__search` → `[probe__search, bundle-mcp, group:plugins]`)
3. **Re-filter** them through the SAME ordered authorization layers that produced the concrete parent tool set — security guarantee: a child can never gain a runtime the parent's policy denies
4. **Preserve** surviving tokens via a new `preserveRuntimeToolAllowlistEntries` option on `replaceWithEffectiveToolAllowlist`

Applied in three code paths: `createOpenClawCodingTools`, `resolveGatewayScopedTools`, and `resolveSkillDispatchTools`.

### Security Guarantee

Runtime tokens are filtered through every policy layer (profile, provider profile, global, agent, group, sender, sandbox, owner-only, subagent, inherited). A subagent policy that narrows the allowlist correctly strips broad tokens like `bundle-mcp` while preserving explicitly-allowed individual MCP/LSP selectors. The deny path works too: a parent that denies `bundle-mcp` prevents any MCP runtime from leaking to children.

## Evidence

### CI / Automated Tests

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-policy.test.ts src/gateway/tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts
```

All 121 tests passed (0 failures).

### New Tests Added (6 total)

| Test file | Tests | What they verify |
|-----------|:-----:|------------------|
| `tool-policy.test.ts` | 3 | Entry identification, policy-layer filtering, deny-layer removal of runtime selectors |
| `tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts` | 2 | Gateway path: token preservation AND narrow-policy filtering |
| `agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts` | 1 | Agent-tools path: token preservation in `createOpenClawCodingTools` |

### Real Behavior Proof

The fix was validated in the same scenario described in #85030:

1. Parent agent configured with `tools.allow` containing `bundle-mcp`, `probe__allowed` (MCP tool), and concrete tools
2. Subagent spawned via `sessions_spawn`
3. Child's `inheritedToolAllow` captured from session store
4. MCP runtime materialized for the child session
5. Child-visible MCP tools = intersection of inherited allowlist and materialized tools

Result: `probe__allowed` was present in the child's tool set; `probe__blocked` (not in the allowlist) was absent. The allowed MCP tool executed successfully via the production tool executor.

### Upstream Reference

Builds on the investigation and proof-of-concept from #92521 by @yu-xin-c.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In a multi-pod / multi-replica deployment, every OpenClaw process exports OTel telemetry under the same identity. The resource only carried `service.name`, with no `service.instance.id`, so collectors and backends cannot tell instances apart — per-pod metrics and traces collapse into one series.

## Approach (reworked after review)

An earlier revision added a custom `OTEL_SERVICE_INSTANCE_ID` env var with an `os.hostname()` fallback. Review correctly flagged that as a security-boundary concern (host identity exported by default) and a non-standard, non-unique default. This revision addresses all of that:

- Resolve `service.instance.id` with precedence: `diagnostics.otel.serviceInstanceId` config field → `OTEL_SERVICE_INSTANCE_ID` env var → **omitted entirely**.
- **No hostname fallback.** When neither source is set, the attribute is not added to the resource, so no host/pod identity is ever exported by default.
- Mirrors how `service.name` is already resolved (config field + env fallback), so it introduces no novel contract — just a symmetric, opt-in identity field.
- Operators who prefer the standard path can still use `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.instance.id=...`.

Docs (`docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md`) document the config field, env var, precedence, and the privacy note (opt-in, opaque, stable, never hostname).

## User Impact

Operators can opt into per-instance identity by setting a stable, opaque id (e.g. a provisioned pod UID) via config or env. Everyone else is unaffected — no attribute is added and no host identity is exposed. No migration required.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof** — the exact resolution + `resourceFromAttributes(...)` logic exercised against the real `@opentelemetry/resources` and `@opentelemetry/semantic-conventions` packages (no mocks), printing the final exported resource attributes for all four cases:

```
1) nothing set
   service.name        = openclaw
   service.instance.id = (absent)
2) config serviceInstanceId set
   service.name        = openclaw
   service.instance.id = pod-config-1
3) OTEL_SERVICE_INSTANCE_ID set
   service.name        = openclaw
   service.instance.id = pod-env-2
4) both set (config wins)
   service.name        = openclaw
   service.instance.id = pod-config-wins
```

This confirms: (1) absent by default (no hostname), (2) config value applied, (3) env value applied, (4) config takes precedence over env.

- `extensions/diagnostics-otel` test suite: **111 passed**, including 4 new tests (omit-by-default, config field, env var, config-wins precedence).
- Branch merged with latest `main` (previous merge conflict resolved).

target.title: fix(update): prevent compatible plugins from being skipped after npm-global upgrades
target.body:
Fixes #93908

## Summary

- Pin current-process post-core plugin update compatibility checks to the installed target OpenClaw version for both upgrades and downgrades.
- Pass the installed target version explicitly into mandatory post-core plugin convergence so it does not overwrite the target with the stale updater process `VERSION`.
- Sync this PR onto current `main` and preserve both the new ClawHub risk-acknowledgement plumbing and this PR's installed-target compatibility source of truth.
- Add regression coverage for the 2026.5.28 -> 2026.6.8 Feishu/plugin API compatibility path.

## What Problem This Solves

- Behavior or issue addressed: Feishu/Lark plugin discovery can be skipped after a package update when post-core plugin update logic still evaluates plugin API compatibility against the pre-update host version. The reported Feishu package declares `openclaw.compat.pluginApi: >=2026.6.8`, but a stale updater process can still report host `2026.5.28`, causing discovery to skip the plugin with `plugin requires plugin API >=2026.6.8, but this host is 2026.5.28; skipping discovery`.
- Why it matters / User impact: Users who update OpenClaw to a Feishu-compatible target can still lose Feishu channel availability because the post-core plugin phase rejects the installed plugin using stale current-process host state. That makes message delivery through Feishu unavailable even though the installed OpenClaw package is new enough.
- What did NOT change: This does not change Feishu package metadata, plugin API ranges, semver compatibility enforcement, plugin manifest parsing, default install choices, ClawHub trust/risk acknowledgement behavior, or runtime fallback behavior for genuinely incompatible plugins.
- Architecture / source-of-truth check: The public contract surface remains `openclaw.compat.pluginApi` and the existing compatibility resolver. The source of truth for post-core update compatibility is the installed target package version because that is the gateway version that will run after restart; this patch only feeds that target version into the existing resolver boundary.
- Related open PR scan: Related open PR #94019 improves compatibility diagnostic guidance, but it does not change discovery/version resolution/update handoff behavior. This PR targets the same-contract root cause in the update handoff rather than duplicating diagnostic text changes.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: The current-process post-core update path could still be running code whose module `VERSION` is the pre-update version (`2026.5.28`) while the installed package root had already been updated to `2026.6.8`. Fresh post-core child processes already receive `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION=<installed target>`, but the current-process path only pinned that override for downgrades. The convergence helper also overwrote inherited compatibility-host state with stale in-process `VERSION`.
- Why this is root-cause fix: Plugin compatibility during post-core update must be evaluated against the installed target package version, not the old updater process module state. Pinning `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION` to the installed target for the current-process plugin phase and passing the same target into convergence restores that lifecycle invariant, so the existing discovery gate makes the same decision the restarted gateway will make instead of masking the symptom with a Feishu-specific exception.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installed target package version is the canonical source of truth for post-core plugin compatibility. This PR scopes the override to the post-core plugin phase and restores the caller's environment afterward, so normal runtime version resolution and explicit operator overrides outside the update handoff are unchanged.

When the installed target package version cannot be read, convergence keeps its previous fallback to the current runtime `VERSION`.

The latest update syncs onto current `main`; conflict resolution keeps main's ClawHub risk acknowledgement options flowing into post-core convergence while also keeping this PR's `compatibilityHostVersion` handoff.

## Verification

- Current-head focused regression command: `pnpm exec vitest run src/cli/update-cli.test.ts -t "pins the compatibility host version"` — 2 passed, 180 skipped.
- Current-head convergence suite: `pnpm exec vitest run src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.test.ts` — 22 passed.
- Target test file: `src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.test.ts` covers the convergence helper using an explicit installed target over stale inherited host state; `src/cli/update-cli.test.ts` covers both current-process upgrade and downgrade paths pinning the environment during post-core plugin update and restoring it afterward.
- Scenario locked in: A package update from process host `2026.5.28` to installed target `2026.6.8` passes `2026.6.8` to plugin convergence and exposes `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION=2026.6.8` only while `updateNpmInstalledPlugins` runs.
- CI repair: the prior head failed `checks-node-compact-small-whole-3` in `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts` because the PR was 211 commits behind `main`; the failure was unrelated to the update diff and reproduced locally. The repository's required `sync-main` flow rebased the patch onto current `main`, which already contains `fix(doctor): restore local audio information (#104281)`. On synced head `7047fbab7264fc74f25951ec5da91522e1a53090`, the exact failing test now passes (1 passed, 90 skipped).

## Real behavior proof

- Existing boundary proof: Windows local worktree with real Feishu package metadata (`@openclaw/feishu@2026.6.8`, `openclaw.compat.pluginApi: >=2026.6.8`). With host `2026.5.28`, Feishu is skipped with `plugin requires plugin API >=2026.6.8, but this host is 2026.5.28`; with installed target `2026.6.8`, the same plugin is discovered without that diagnostic.
- Strong lifecycle proof attempted on current head: build a PR tarball, install it through a disposable npm-global prefix, retain `@openclaw/feishu@2026.6.8`, downgrade core to `2026.5.28`, then invoke `openclaw update --tag <candidate> --yes --json` without `--no-restart` or a manual compatibility-host override and verify the restarted gateway discovers Feishu.
- Environment limitation: this Windows host has neither Docker nor a disposable VM. Candidate packaging also could not complete: the repository build exhausted the available V8 heap near 8 GB during `tsdown`, before a tarball was produced. Therefore this update does **not** claim that the requested npm-global update/restart lifecycle proof completed.
- Required follow-up proof remains: a disposable Windows managed-service or equivalent systemd run showing baseline `2026.5.28`, retained Feishu `2026.6.8`, absent `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION`, update-owned package replacement and restart, target-version health verification, successful post-restart Feishu runtime inspection, and the compatibility override still absent afterward.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** Still open as a proof request. The exact npm-global update/restart proof was attempted but the available host could not package or run the disposable managed-service scenario.
- **RF-002:** The production lifecycle value remains high impact; focused current-head tests verify selection, scope, and restoration, but they are not presented as a substitute for live lifecycle evidence.
- **RF-003:** Still open. Existing real output manually selects the compatibility host and therefore proves only the discovery decision boundary, not the patched update handoff or post-restart result.
- **RF-004:** No additional mechanical code defect was identified. Maintainer review still needs either the requested external lifecycle transcript or an explicit decision to accept boundary-level evidence.

## Regression Test Plan

- Fix classification: Root-cause fix for the update/plugin convergence version handoff; it changes the source-of-truth handoff used by existing compatibility checks rather than adding a Feishu-specific exception.
- Patch quality notes: The only type escape touched here is the pre-existing test style for constructing a minimal `OpenClawConfig` fixture (`as unknown as OpenClawConfig`); production code does not add a type escape. Patch-quality warning handling is explicit: this is not a guard/default/catch fallback, and the code changes the lifecycle source of truth used by existing compatibility checks.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High for the stale-version handoff and discovery decision boundary because the production path has focused regression tests plus real Feishu metadata discovery proof. The lower-confidence area is external Feishu network delivery, which is disclosed as not tested.

## Merge risk

- Risk labels considered: `merge-risk:availability`, `merge-risk:compatibility`, `merge-risk:update`, `merge-risk:plugin-runtime`.
- Risk explanation: Post-core update compatibility checks affect installed external plugin update/discovery behavior and therefore plugin availability after update. The change is intentionally narrow: during the post-core plugin phase, use the installed target package version that will run after restart. It does not relax compatibility checks, does not change public config/schema/protocol, and does not introduce a new config/env surface.
- Why acceptable: The fresh child process already uses this installed-target-version contract. This PR makes the current-process path and convergence helper follow the same contract, restores the previous environment after the scoped phase, preserves main's ClawHub risk acknowledgement flow, and preserves the existing runtime `VERSION` fallback if the target version cannot be read.

## Non-goals

- Do not change Feishu package metadata or plugin API requirements.
- Do not relax or bypass plugin API compatibility checks.
- Do not add runtime fallbacks for incompatible plugins.

![Composer with image and pasted text attachments](https://calm-mill-vpd8.here.now/pasted-text-with-image.png)

![Composer with pasted text attachment only](https://calm-mill-vpd8.here.now/pasted-text-only.png)

## Summary

This changes the Control UI composer so plain-text pastes over 1000 characters become compact `text/plain` attachments instead of filling the textarea.

The attachment uses the existing chat attachment payload path. When the user sends it, the chat request includes the pasted text as a file attachment with `mimeType: "text/plain"`; when the user clicks “Show in text field”, the attachment is removed and the full paste is restored into the composer draft as normal message text.

Short text pastes still behave like normal textarea input. Image pastes still use the existing image attachment flow.

## Details

- Converts long plain-text paste events into `pasted-text-*.txt` composer attachments.
- Shows a compact attachment card with a short preview from the pasted text.
- Keeps the default composer placeholder for pasted-text-only attachments.
- Uses the same remove button treatment for image and pasted-text attachments.
- Preserves the existing attachment send path for retry, queueing, cleanup, and payload serialization.

## Validation

target.title: fix: webChat scrollback history is too limited — older assistant replies and tool outputs disappear when scrolling…
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Fixes an issue where users paginating session history could never reach a compaction marker that the full history reader included before the active transcript branch.**
- **Affected surface / workflow:** Gateway/session history JSONL indexing and offset pagination used by history consumers.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** The full reader preserves the nearest compaction record before an explicitly selected active branch, but the byte-offset transcript index built its active view from branch nodes only. Pagination therefore indexed three visible rows where the full reader exposed four.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** `totalMessages` and message `seq` values were shifted, and no offset could retrieve the compaction boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Complete shipped solution:** One shared transcript-tree selector now owns active-branch plus nearest-preceding-compaction selection, and both the full/bounded filesystem reader and byte-offset index consume it before assigning sequence numbers or serving pages.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** Counts, sequence metadata, identity lookups, and pages all derive from the transcript index; correcting its active-entry selection restores one consistent visible-history invariant rather than patching pagination output downstream.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** `src/config/sessions/transcript-tree.ts` owns active transcript selection for all filesystem readers. It selects the normalized active path and nearest preceding compaction once; `session-utils.fs.ts` and `session-transcript-index.fs.ts` only adapt their record wrappers to that canonical helper.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** No protocol/schema/UI changes, no new cursor semantics, and no change to linear transcripts or all-entry identity lookup.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** This is an additive correction to existing history contents and metadata. Open PR #87111 adds broader WebChat cursor pagination and active-branch indexing work; this PR is intentionally separate and narrower because its current implementation does not preserve the pre-branch compaction row in the index. If #87111 lands, this invariant should be retained during integration.
- **Related open PR scan:** #87111 was inspected at current head `394564241690`; it implements cursor/UI pagination but its active index path still selects only branch nodes, so it does not cover the compaction-before-active-branch edge case. Other related PRs surfaced by the issue workflow do not make current `main` behavior equivalent to this fix.
- **Out of scope:** WebChat controls, Gateway protocol fields, page-size policy, display projection, imported CLI history, and cursor design remain owned by #87111 or later work.
- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: session-state` and `merge-risk: availability`.
- **Risk explanation:** The transcript index is shared by count, full async, and paginated history readers, so changing active-entry selection can affect visible history metadata. The change only restores the nearest compaction row already exposed by the synchronous full reader and leaves branch-message filtering unchanged.
- **Why acceptable:** The fix makes all production readers agree on one existing visible-history invariant, is covered with a real branched JSONL fixture, and changes no API, schema, persistence format, or fallback behavior.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** Page all the way back to the compaction marker and observe `totalMessages`/`seq` values matching full history for the same JSONL transcript.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** Active-branch filtering still excludes abandoned and side-branch messages; only the already-visible compaction boundary is restored to the indexed view.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** No browser UI proof was needed because this fix is below the UI/protocol layer. The production filesystem full and paginated readers were exercised directly against the same real JSONL file.

## Evidence

- **Environment:** Windows Git Bash, Node 22.17.0, pnpm 11.2.2. The branch was synced through the required daily-fix `sync-main` flow after drift analysis found a real merge conflict and dependency-file changes across 212 upstream commits.
- **Commands run after this patch:** focused `src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts`; exact formerly failing `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`; a production-path TypeScript script calling `readSessionMessages` and `readSessionMessagesPageWithStatsAsync` against one on-disk JSONL; `git diff --check`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** write one branched session JSONL containing an abandoned branch, a compaction marker, the selected active branch, a side branch, and a leaf selector; call the production full reader once; then call the production paginated reader with `maxMessages=1` at offsets 0 through 4; compare visible rows, `totalMessages`, and `seq` values.
- **Observed result after fix:** Before the fix, full history returned 4 rows with compaction `seq=1`, while pagination reported `totalMessages=3`, shifted active rows to `seq=1..3`, and could not retrieve compaction at any offset. On the synced fixed head, pagination reports `totalMessages=4`; offsets 0/1/2 return active rows at `seq=4/3/2`; offset 3 returns compaction `seq=1`; offset 4 is empty. Gateway coverage passed 388/388. The old CI failure was unrelated to this PR, and the exact doctor-health suite now passes 91/91.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** `RF-001` waiting-on-author is addressed by this update. `RF-002` and `RF-005` fixed — full/bounded and indexed readers now use one canonical selector in `transcript-tree.ts`. `RF-003` fixed — the closing footer was replaced with a non-closing related-work reference. `RF-004` documented — #87111 integration must retain this shared selector and regression invariant. `RF-006` passed — Gateway suite 388/388. `RF-007` passed — `git diff --check` is clean.
- **Target regression test:** the branched real-JSONL case in `src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts`.
- **Regression scenario:** compaction immediately precedes the selected active branch while abandoned and side-branch messages remain excluded.
- **Why this test is a guardrail:** it fails if compaction disappears again, if offsets cannot reach it, or if `totalMessages`/`seq` diverge between full and paginated readers.
- **Regression guardrail:** `src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts` locks a branched real-JSONL scenario where compaction immediately precedes the selected active branch; it is the smallest reliable guard because it simultaneously verifies active-branch filtering, compaction reachability, offsets, `totalMessages`, and sequence assignment through the production reader.
- **Unavailable environment disclosure:** the workflow reports no local Gateway daemon proof capability. A daemon/browser is not part of this filesystem-reader boundary; instead, the actual production full and paginated reader functions were executed against a real on-disk JSONL, with exact output included above.
- **Patch quality notes:** Two-file focused change; no fallback, protocol expansion, generated files, dependencies, or lockfile changes.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for this narrow invariant; production reader proof and regression coverage agree.

Related to #92317; this PR restores the compaction/index invariant, while broader WebChat cursor and older-history loading remains tracked separately.

## What Problem This Solves

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA Lab Telegram live progress output can contain malformed text when a detail message has emoji at the 240-character truncation boundary.

Telegram QA progress details remain well-formed when scenario or canary diagnostics contain long emoji-containing values.

### Regression test crosses the actual cut
The test now uses a 236-code-unit ASCII prefix followed by emoji+after. **After fix** (`truncateUtf16Safe`):
- Truncated: 236 `a` (backed up to avoid splitting surrogate pair)
- Final output: 236 `a` + `...` (239 code units)

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(agents): distinguish z.ai code 1305 content rejection from generic overload
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: z.ai Coding Plan endpoint returns HTTP 429 with code 1305 deterministically when the system prompt contains "You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw". The current error classifier treats all 1305 responses as generic overload, showing "The AI service is temporarily overloaded" to users — which is misleading for the content-rejection case.

**Solution**: Add a `ZAI_CODE_1305_RE` pattern to detect `{"code":1305,...}` or `{"code":"1305",...}` (quoted or unquoted) in the raw error message and surface a more specific diagnostic before falling back to the generic overload message. The `classifyFailoverReason` hook in the z.ai plugin ensures code 1305 is classified as "overloaded" (provider-scoped), preventing misclassification by the generic rate-limit pattern.

**What changed**: 
- `sanitize-user-facing-text.ts`: Updated `ZAI_CODE_1305_RE` regex constant to match both `"code":1305` (unquoted number) and `"code":"1305"` (quoted string) JSON values; new check in `formatRateLimitOrOverloadedErrorCopy` that runs before `isOverloadedErrorMessage` and returns a neutral diagnostic for z.ai 1305 errors: "transient overload or a provider-side content restriction — try again later or with a different model."
- `extensions/zai/index.ts`: Added `classifyFailoverReason` hook that explicitly classifies z.ai code 1305 as "overloaded" (provider-scoped, prevents generic rate-limit classification from bypassing the diagnostic check)
- `failover-matches.test.ts`, `formatassistanterrortext.test.ts`: Updated tests to expect the new diagnostic message

**What did NOT change**:
- The `rate_limit` failover classification is preserved — backoff and fallback continue working
- Non-1305 overload errors return the original "overloaded" message unchanged
- Zhipu GLM `[1305]` format is not affected (doesn't match the JSON key pattern)

**Fixes**: #103529

## What Problem This Solves

Users onboarding a valid z.ai Coding Plan key successfully, but every chat turn fails with a misleading "overloaded" error. The real cause — the system prompt signature line triggering a provider-side content filter — is invisible. Users waste time checking quota, retrying, or switching API keys when the issue is the system prompt content.

## Root Cause

z.ai's Coding Plan endpoint returns HTTP 429 with `{"error":{"code":"1305","message":"The service may be temporarily overloaded, please try again later."}}` when the system message contains "You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw". This behavior is a **deterministic function of the system prompt content**, not a transient overload. Removing or altering that one line produces a 200 response.

The error classifier in `sanitize-user-facing-text.ts` matched the "overloaded" keyword in the response body and returned the generic overload message, which is incorrect for this scenario.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Error message for z.ai code 1305 now mentions possible content restriction instead of generic overload

**Real environment tested**: Node 24, macOS, tsx 4.19, vitest 4.1.9

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Direct call to `formatRateLimitOrOverloadedErrorCopy` (production function) via tsx — covering canonical payload, backward-compatible format, and non-1305 fallthrough.

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal
$ node --import tsx zai-1305-evidence.ts
=== Part 1: Canonical payload ===
Input: {"error":{"code":"1305","message":"The service may be temporarily..."}}
Output: ⚠️ Provider returned code 1305. This can be a transient overload
or a provider-side content restriction — try again later or with a
different model.

=== Part 2: Backward compatible ===
Input: {"code":1305,"message":"..."}
Output: ⚠️ Provider returned code 1305. [same diagnostic]

=== Part 3: Non-1305 fallthrough ===
Generic overload: "The AI service is temporarily overloaded." ← unchanged
Rate limit with retry: "⚠️ rate limit: service overloaded..." ← preserved
Zhipu GLM [1305]: undefined ← not affected
Non-z.ai 429: "⚠️ API rate limit reached." ← passes through
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The diagnostic is more neutral — it covers both overload and content-rejection scenarios without misleading users toward "system prompt" guidance they cannot act on. Provider-scoping through the z.ai plugin's `classifyFailoverReason` hook prevents the generic rate-limit classifier from bypassing the diagnostic check.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end with a real z.ai API key (L3 full gateway run). The original issue (#103529) provides curl-level reproduction. L2 real-module execution (tsx directly calling the exported function) covers all payload formats the formatter is designed to handle.

## Tests and validation

**Exact steps or command run**: vitest run (32 + 90 + 15 tests)

**Test output**:

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a memory spike in the Gemini embedding batch download step where large batch output files are fully buffered in memory before any embedding is written to the result map.

`fetchGeminiFileContent` called `res.text()` to download the JSONL output file as a single string, then `parseGeminiBatchOutput` called `text.split("\n")` to produce a full `GeminiBatchOutputLine[]` array. Both the raw text buffer and the parsed object array exist simultaneously at peak — for a large embedding batch this roughly doubles peak heap on top of the result map.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the two-step buffer-then-parse approach with a streaming readline reader that consumes one JSONL line at a time and writes each embedding directly into `byCustomId`, matching the pattern already established in `extensions/voyage/embedding-batch.ts`.

Structural changes:

- **Deleted** `fetchGeminiFileContent` — returned the full JSONL body as a `string`.
- **Deleted** `parseGeminiBatchOutput` — split the string and mapped it to `GeminiBatchOutputLine[]`.
- **Added** `readGeminiBatchOutputContent` — wraps `Response.body` with `Readable.fromWeb` + `readline.Interface`, applies each line inline, and always closes/destroys reader resources in `finally`.
- **Added** `fetchGeminiBatchOutput` — thin wrapper that builds the `:download` URL and delegates body reading to the streamed reader.

Identifier precedence (`key` / `custom_id` / `request_id`) and both error paths are preserved.

## User Impact

Peak memory for large Gemini embedding batch jobs drops from roughly `2× output file size` (raw text + parsed lines + result map) toward approximately the embedding result map size. Successful batches, partial-error batches, and empty-output error paths keep the same user-visible behavior.

## Evidence

- Pattern parity with `extensions/voyage/embedding-batch.ts` streamed JSONL reader
- Focused regression: delayed mid-line chunked `ReadableStream` body through production `runGeminiEmbeddingBatches`
- Real `node:http` Transfer-Encoding chunked download against production caller with peak-heap before/after

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Gemini embedding batch download no longer holds the full JSONL text and a full parsed-line array in memory at the same time while populating `byCustomId`.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `runGeminiEmbeddingBatches` → `fetchGeminiBatchOutput` → `withRemoteHttpResponse` → `readGeminiBatchOutputContent` (`Readable.fromWeb` + `readline`) → per-line `byCustomId.set`.

- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Mirrors Voyage's provider-local streamed JSONL reader; no new config/env. Google Batch API output remains JSONL with per-line `key`/`response`/`error`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin 24.3.0), Node 22 (`--expose-gc --import tsx`), branch `fix/gemini-batch-streaming-jsonl-reader`.

```text
$ node --expose-gc --import tsx /tmp/gemini-batch-stream-proof.mjs
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google/embedding-batch.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running OpenAI Codex device-code login (`openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code`, or the equivalent configure/wizard auth choice) could hang forever when a single `auth.openai.com` HTTP request stopped responding.

Before this patch, the flow only enforced a 15-minute poll-loop deadline around authorization waiting. The three `fetch` calls for user-code request, authorization poll, and token exchange had no per-request `AbortSignal` timeout, so a stalled TCP/proxy/blackhole response could bypass that deadline and leave the CLI spinner stuck. A server that returned headers and then stalled the body could also escape an incomplete timeout catch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Treat each device-code HTTP call as one timed operation: headers fetch plus bounded body read under the same `AbortSignal.timeout` (30s, aligned with the sibling ChatGPT browser OAuth token request timeout). Poll requests clamp that timeout to the remaining 15-minute authorization deadline and retry on per-operation timeout (including post-header body stalls) until the overall deadline expires. User-code and token-exchange timeouts fail fast with a clear error.

Scope stays OpenAI Codex device-code login HTTP only; browser OAuth and other providers are unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung device-code HTTP request (or a post-header body stall) could block `models auth login --device-code` indefinitely, even past the advertised 15-minute authorization window.

**After:** Each device-code request+body read aborts after 30 seconds (or sooner near the overall deadline). Poll timeouts retry within the 15-minute window; user-code and token-exchange stalls surface an explicit timeout error instead of hanging forever.

## Evidence

- `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.ts` — one operation deadline for fetch + body read on user-code, poll, and token-exchange; poll retries on timeout within the 15-minute deadline
- Regression: `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts`
  - hung user-code aborts with timeout error
  - poll retries after `TimeoutError` and completes
  - hung token exchange aborts with timeout error
  - success path asserts all three fetches carry an `AbortSignal`
  - real `node:http` partial-body stall: user-code / token-exchange abort with formatted timeout; poll retries and succeeds

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenAI Codex device-code login no longer leaves individual HTTP operations unbounded when the remote endpoint stops responding before headers return, or returns headers and then stalls the body.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Operator runs device-code auth → `loginOpenAICodexDeviceCode` → `requestOpenAICodexDeviceCode` / `pollOpenAICodexDeviceCode` / `exchangeOpenAICodexDeviceCode` → `runOpenAICodexDeviceCodeRequest` (`fetch` + `readOpenAICodexDeviceBody` under `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`).
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; production device-code helpers exercised via colocated Vitest against a real hanging `node:http` loopback that sends headers then a partial JSON prefix and never finishes the body. Only `AbortSignal.timeout` duration is shortened for deterministic proof; the production fetch+body composition and error/retry mapping stay unmocked.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Matches the existing 30s OpenAI ChatGPT OAuth token request timeout; uses `AbortSignal.timeout` like GitHub Copilot device-flow request timeouts. Does not migrate this path onto `fetchWithSsrFGuard` in this change.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node 22, product checkout on branch `fix/openai-device-code-request-timeout`.

target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Google Chat webhook authentication could hang indefinitely when Google's signing-certificate endpoint accepts a connection but never completes the HTTP response.

This path runs on cold start and again every 10 minutes when the cert cache expires, so a stalled `googleapis.com` request blocks all incoming Google Chat message verification until the gateway process is restarted.

Outbound Google Chat API timeouts were already addressed in #102227; this PR closes the remaining unbounded fetch in the inbound auth path. Related but distinct from #103627, which bounds the shared Gaxios Google-auth transport rather than this direct webhook certificate fetch.

Related: #5126

## Why This Change Was Made

`fetchChatCerts()` in `extensions/googlechat/src/auth.ts` called `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a deadline. The fix adds a 30-second `timeoutMs` via a local `GOOGLECHAT_AUTH_TIMEOUT_MS` constant, matching the deadline already used for outbound Chat API calls and sibling channel auth paths.

No config/env knobs were added. The shared Gaxios transport timeout remains separate complementary work (#103627).

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled cert endpoint leaves webhook auth pending forever; incoming Google Chat messages fail silently with no timeout error and no lane release.

**After:** Cert fetch aborts after 30 seconds with a concrete error; verification returns `{ ok: false, reason: ... }` and the gateway can continue processing other traffic.

## Evidence

- `extensions/googlechat/src/auth.ts` — `GOOGLECHAT_AUTH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` passed as `timeoutMs` to `fetchWithSsrFGuard` in `fetchChatCerts()`
- Regression: `extensions/googlechat/src/auth.test.ts`

  - surfaces `{ ok: false, reason: /aborted/i }` when the guard rejects with `AbortError`
- Target-level assertion updated in `extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Direct Google Chat webhook certificate retrieval no longer waits forever when the cert endpoint accepts TCP but never returns response bytes.
- **Canonical reachability path:**

```text
inbound Google Chat webhook (project-number audience)
  → verifyGoogleChatRequest
  → fetchChatCerts
  → fetchWithSsrFGuard({ url: CHAT_CERTS_URL, timeoutMs: 30_000 })
  → buildTimeoutAbortSignal deadline aborts stalled request
  → { ok: false, reason: ... }
```

- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; production `verifyGoogleChatRequest` → `fetchChatCerts` through the real unmocked `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against a controlled hanging `node:http` loopback. The `googleapis.com` cert URL keeps the real SSRF hostname allowlist satisfied; only `globalThis.fetch` is redirected onto the loopback origin so the guard's composed timeout signal rides the real request.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Deadline matches outbound Google Chat API timeout and sibling auth control-plane paths (30s). Does not change Gaxios Google-auth transport (#103627) or outbound Chat control/media (#102227).
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin), Node via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs`, branch `fix/googlechat-api-request-timeout`, exact head after squash/rebase onto `upstream/main`.

- Real `fetchWithSsrFGuard` schedules the production 30s deadline via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`
- Loopback server confirms the cert request arrived and never responds
- Mutation control: without firing the deadline, verification stays `pending` past 500ms
- Firing the captured production deadline aborts the in-flight request; `verifyGoogleChatRequest` returns `{ ok: false, reason: /aborted|timed out|timeout/i }`

## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `cron.sessionRetention: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolveRetentionMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and `sweepCronRunSessions` computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all cron run sessions for immediate deletion.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` to reject any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Added a registered legacy rule + migration that uses `parseDurationMs` (same `{ defaultUnit: "h" }` options as schema) in both detection and repair paths. This covers all parser-equivalent zero representations — `"0"`, `"0h"`, `"0d"`, `"0ms"`, `"0s"`, `"0m"`, `"0.0h"`, `"0h0m"`, `"0h0m0s"`, etc. The migration removes only values that parse to ≤ 0 so the documented 24h default applies; positive durations, `false`, and unparseable strings are preserved.

target.title: fix(memory-core): guard catch-block async calls and supplement search against unhandled rejections
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three untracked async-rejection paths exist in memory-core where a function called without its own error guard can throw, causing the rejection to escape the enclosing context as an unhandled promise rejection.

### 1. `activateFallbackProvider` — called from inside `catch` blocks, throws when dual-provider creation fails

Both `ensureSourceWideSync` and `runMemoryTargetedSessionSync` catch embedding errors and attempt to activate a fallback provider via `activateFallbackProvider()`. Inside that method, `createEmbeddingProvider()` can throw when both the primary and the fallback provider fail. Since `activateFallbackProvider` has no try-catch around the provider creation call, the error propagates out of the caller's catch block as an unhandled rejection instead of being treated as a failed fallback attempt.

### 2. `getSupplementMemoryReadResult` in `corpus=wiki` — untracked promise rejection from supplement `get()`

The `memory_get` tool's `corpus=wiki` branch calls `getSupplementMemoryReadResult()` without any try-catch. Previously failures could be reported as indistinguishable "not found"; now the actual backend error is surfaced.

### 3. `searchMemoryCorpusSupplements` — supplement search discarded all results when one failed

If any single supplement's `search()` throws, results from healthy supplements were discarded. Additionally, when ALL registered supplements fail, the error is now propagated so unavailable-phase handling returns an explicit unavailable result instead of silently reporting empty success.

## Changes

- `manager-sync-ops.ts`: `.catch()` on `createEmbeddingProvider` in `activateFallbackProvider` → returns `false` on failure instead of throwing
- `tools.ts corpus=wiki`: try-catch with `formatErrorMessage()` → surfaces actual backend failure, not "not found"
- `tools.shared.ts searchMemoryCorpusSupplements`: per-supplement try-catch with failure-count → isolates broken supplements; throws on all-fail for unavailable signal

## Evidence

**TypeScript:** clean on all changed files.

**Unit tests (26/26 passed):**

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
```

### Gateway live proof (P1)

Isolated local Gateway + `memory-core` + `memory-wiki` environment. Plugins loaded: `memory-core`, `memory-wiki`, `proof-broken-corpus` (search throws), plus workspace memory seed.

```

date: 2026-07-11T13:25:07Z
gateway: ws://127.0.0.1:19001 (loopback, token auth)
state: <PROOF_STATE_DIR>
wiki vault: <PROOF_STATE_DIR>/wiki (seed page id: source.alpha)
```

**P1-A — `memory_search corpus=all` (one failing + one healthy supplement):**

```bash
openclaw gateway call tools.invoke \
  --token <redacted> \
  --params '{"name":"memory_search","args":{"query":"alpha","corpus":"all"},"agentId":"main"}' --json
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "toolName": "memory_search",
  "output": {
    "details": {
      "results": [
        {
          "corpus": "wiki",
          "path": "sources/alpha.md",
          "title": "Alpha",
          "kind": "source",
          "id": "source.alpha"
        },
        {
          "corpus": "memory",
          "path": "MEMORY.md",
          "startLine": 1,
          "endLine": 7,
          "citation": "MEMORY.md#L1-L7"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "source": "plugin"
}
```

Healthy wiki supplement result preserved while `proof-broken-corpus` search failure is isolated (no all-fail unavailable).

**P1-B — `memory_get corpus=wiki` (healthy wiki supplement):**

```bash
openclaw gateway call tools.invoke \
  --token <redacted> \
  --params '{"name":"memory_get","args":{"path":"source.alpha","corpus":"wiki","from":1,"lines":15},"agentId":"main"}' --json
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "toolName": "memory_get",
  "output": {
    "details": {
      "corpus": "wiki",
      "path": "sources/alpha.md",
      "title": "Alpha",
      "kind": "source",
      "id": "source.alpha",
      "fromLine": 1,
      "lineCount": 15,
      "truncated": true,
      "text": "\n# Alpha\n\n## Source\n- Type: `local-file`\n..."
    }
  },
  "source": "plugin"
}
```

**P1-C — `memory_get corpus=wiki` (supplement backend throws):**

Config: wiki disabled; external plugin `proof-broken-get` registers a corpus supplement whose `get()` throws.

```bash
openclaw gateway call tools.invoke \
  --token <redacted> \
  --params '{"name":"memory_get","args":{"path":"source.alpha","corpus":"wiki"},"agentId":"main"}' --json
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "toolName": "memory_get",
  "output": {
    "details": {
      "path": "source.alpha",
      "text": "",
      "disabled": true,
      "error": "proof-broken-get corpus get failed"
    }
  },
  "source": "plugin"
}
```

Backend failure surfaced via `formatErrorMessage()` path; not reported as a generic healthy empty read.

**Summary of changes by file:**

| File | Change | Lines |
|------|--------|-------|
| `manager-sync-ops.ts` | `.catch()` on `createEmbeddingProvider` | +6/-0 |
| `tools.ts` | try-catch wiki get, surfaces actual error | +6/-1 |
| `tools.shared.ts` | per-supplement try-catch + failure-count, throws on all-fail | +8/-0 |
| `tools.citations.test.ts` | 3 proof tests | +99/-0 |

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
